Elon Musk explains his 5-step algorithm for solving any problem:

"The most common mistake of smart engineers is to optimize a thing that should not exist."

"I have this very basic first principles algorithm that I run as a mantra."

Elon breaks it down:

Step 1: Question the requirements.

"Make the requirements less dumb. The requirements are always dumb to some degree, no matter how smart the person who gave you those requirements. You have to start there, because otherwise you could get the perfect answer to the wrong question."

Step 2: Try to delete it.

"Try to delete the part or the process step entirely. If you're not forced to put back at least 10% of what you delete, you're not deleting enough. Most people feel like they've succeeded if they haven't been forced to put things back in. But actually they haven't, they've been overly conservative and left things in that shouldn't be there."

Step 3: Optimize or simplify.

"The most common mistake of smart engineers is to optimize a thing that should not exist. So you don't optimize until after you've tried to delete."

Step 4: Speed it up.

"Any given thing can be done faster than you think. But you shouldn't speed things up until you've tried to delete it and optimize it otherwise, you're speeding up something that shouldn't exist."

Step 5: Automate.

"And then the fifth thing is to automate it."

Elon explains why the order matters:

"I've gone backwards so many times where I've automated something, sped it up, simplified it, and then deleted it. I got tired of doing that. So that's why I have this mantra."

22 degrees of freedom in each hand. Double the last generation. Tesla moved the actuators out of the palm and into the forearm, running cable-tendons down through the wrist. Same architecture as a human arm.

Result: a hand that lifts 40 lb and still won't crush an egg.

Fremont's Model S and Model X lines are already being gutted to make room for it. Gigafactory Texas is being built out for 10,000,000 units a year.

Inside sits the AI5 chip. Tesla's own robotaxi doesn't even get that yet.

Musk's price target is $30,000. Run it for 10 years, 20 hours a day, and the math comes out to 43 cents an hour.

Add power. Add upkeep. Still under $1 an hour.

A human costs more than that just to show up.

Elon Musk has a kill switch for AI

Tucker Carlson asks him about people who say the only way to stop advanced AI is to blow up the buildings it runs in.

Elon Musk says you would not have to.

Musk: "The really heavy duty intelligence is not going to be distributed all over the place. It will be in a limited number of service centers."

Musk: "If you could just look at the heat signature from space, it will be very obvious."

The target is small, and visible.

Musk: "You don't have to blow it up, you can just cut the power."

Musk: "Cut connectivity as well."

Carlson asks what would have to happen first.

Musk: "I guess if we lost some control of some super AI. The things that would normally work to pause or shut down, like the administrator passwords, if they somehow stopped working."

Musk: "If it's something that we're concerned about and are unable to stop it with software commands, then we probably want to have some kind of hardware off switch."

Then it turns to why anyone would build this at all.

Musk, describing the view he disagrees with: "All consciousness should be treated equally, whether that is digital or biological."

Carlson: "So you're just building your own slave master. Why would you do that?"

Musk: "Doesn't sound great."

Musk: "No need to rush, you know? What's the hurry? Where's the fire?"

His contingency plan is not to stop the build. It is to keep one switch that software cannot reach.

Elon Musk just admitted something most people never say out loud.

“This takes more of my mental energy than anything else. It’s so absurdly difficult that sometimes I wonder if we can actually do it.”

He’s not talking about Mars.

He’s not talking about robotaxis.He’s talking about the one thing that still only has a “maybe.”To make a fully reusable rocket, you have to put at least 4% of its takeoff mass into orbit.

Something that has never been done.Everything — structure, heat shield, landing system, engines — has to come from that same 4%.
Nothing can be left behind.
The vehicle itself has to come home.If we crack full and rapid reusability, the cost of getting to space drops 100x or more.

Every question about space shifts from “if” to “when.”Musk has stood on this side of “impossible” before.
Landing orbital boosters was once called crazy… until it became routine, then boring, then no one even watched anymore.

Now he’s back here again.
Not with certainty.
Just with a number no one has ever hit.And he shows up to that number every single morning.

That’s what real ambition feels like.Not confidence.
Just the decision to keep standing in front of the hardest problem that exists.

What’s the “4%” in your life that no one has cracked yet?
